chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Harun ibn Muslim, from Mas'ada ibn Sadaqa, from Abu Abdillah, from his forefathers (peace be upon them), that Ali (peace be upon him) was saying:
Regarding a man who became Muslim during the middle of the month of Ramadan, that there is nothing upon him except for what he faces coming.

key_terms.مَا يَسْتَقْبِلُ: What he faces coming / The remaining period

ai.seo_question: What are the prayer obligations for someone who converts to Islam in the middle of Ramadan?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that a new Muslim entering during Ramadan is exempt from making up missed prayers, as the obligation begins from the moment of conversion. This ruling highlights the principle of gradual obligation in Shia jurisprudence, distinguishing between the duty to pray and the duty to fast, which may require separate consideration. The narration underscores the mercy and practicality of divine law for those newly embracing the faith.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from Haroun Bin Muslim, from Mas’ada Bin Sadaqa, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, from his<sup>asws</sup> forefathers<sup>asws</sup> that Ali<sup>asws</sup> was saying
regarding a man who became a Muslim during half of the Month of Ramazan that there is nothing upon him except for what he faces coming’.
en.sarwar: 2. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from Harun ibn Muslim from Mas’adah ibn Sadaqah who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that ’Amir al-Mu’minin, Ali ‘Alayhi al-Salam,
about one who accepts Islam in the middle of the month of Ramadan would say that he is not obligated for anything of fasting except for the coming days.”
